title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: call quality feedback surveys after meetings
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly leaves the underlying Teams Rooms licence prerequisite open, although Microsoft documents it. The Cloud Policy navigation also skips a required setup page; the feature's default and roadmap details are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing call quality feedback surveys for Teams Rooms on Android.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is introducing call quality feedback (CQF) surveys for Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can rate calls and meetings and give feedback about call, video, audio and screen-sharing quality.
claims.quote: These surveys allow users to rate the quality of calls and meetings and provide feedback about audio, video, and screen-sharing experiences.

claims.claim: Users periodically see the survey after meetings end on Teams Rooms on Android devices.
claims.quote: Users will periodically see a call quality feedback survey after meetings end on Teams Rooms on Android devices.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the purpose as helping organisations ensure consistent, high-quality experiences.
claims.quote: provide additional feedback on calling, video, and screen-sharing experiences to help organizations ensure consistent, high-quality experiences.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk

claims.quote: The feature becomes available after eligible Teams Rooms on Android devices are updated to the required app version.

claims.quote: No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'The feature asks users to rate calls and meetings and provide feedback to Microsoft.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.quote: Searched: "Teams Rooms" "call quality" "survey" licensing price charge meter. Read MC1490912, the roadmap, rooms-manage, both feedback policy pages, overview-cloud-policy and rooms-plan; no survey-specific licence, meter or charge found.

Remove the final Open questions bullet and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-plan.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.claim: Managing devices in the Teams admin center requires Teams Administrator or Teams Devices Administrator.

claims.claim: The creation path is Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Create > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select Next.
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[0].ui and the rendered table with 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings'. The existing path skips the required naming page as well as scope selection.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell, Graph or other API to configure this Cloud Policy survey control.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 PowerShell Graph API create policy configuration surveys; "Cloud Policy" "API" "surveys". Read overview-cloud-policy and both feedback policy pages; no Cloud Policy configuration command or endpoint found.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy is documented for suppressing Teams Rooms in-product surveys, including call quality prompts, with Android-specific suppression left for pilot confirmation.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms devices may display in-product surveys, including call quality feedback prompts, to signed-in room accounts. To disable these surveys, use the Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy control has user scope.
claims.quote: Policies only apply to user objects.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Allow users to receive and respond to in-product surveys from Microsoft is the setting controlling whether surveys appear.
claims.quote: | Allow users to receive and respond to in-product surveys from Microsoft | Controls whether surveys appear within product. |

claims.claim: Not Configured has the same effect as Enabled for the survey policy, so leaving it unconfigured does not suppress surveys.
claims.quote: When the following policies are set to Not Configured, it has the same effect as if you set the policies to Enabled.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Office Apps Administrator for Cloud Policy management.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended)

claims.claim: Feedback policy changes can take a few hours to reach client applications.
claims.quote: After you apply policies, it can take a few hours for the client applications to update.
